s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal condition with signs of peritonitis and sepsis following intestinal surgery
salient_findings: Total abdominal tenderness with rebound pain and muscle tension
Intestinal perforation and peritonitis on CT scan
key_facts: 29-year-old Chinese male patient
No underlying disease
Hospitalized twice for injuries from a car accident
Initial admission for open abdominal injury
Emergency surgery and discharge after 5 days
Re-admitted due to persistent lower abdominal pain
Underwent emergency surgery for intestinal issues
Temperature rose to 39.3°C post-surgery
WBC 16.62 x109/L and neutrophils 87.80% on second admission
WBC 22.68 x109/L and neutrophils 94.1% post-surgery
CT scan showed intestinal perforation, peritonitis, and thickening of ascending colon and ileum segments
Blood culture positive in bilateral anaerobic bottles
Gram stain showed Gram-negative bacteria
Culture showed slow-growing, moist, gray-white colonies after 3 days

shortlist.label: Postoperative peritonitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has signs of peritonitis and sepsis following intestinal surgery

shortlist.label: Sepsis due to gram-negative bacteria
shortlist.why_kept: Blood culture positive for gram-negative bacteria and patient has high fever

shortlist.label: Intra-abdominal abscess
shortlist.why_kept: CT scan showed intestinal perforation and peritonitis, which can lead to abscess formation

shortlist.label: Bacteroides fragilis infection
shortlist.why_kept: Gram stain showed gram-negative bacteria and patient has intestinal perforation, which can lead to Bacteroides fragilis infection

shortlist.label: Enterococcal peritonitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has peritonitis and enterococcal peritonitis is a possible cause of peritonitis in abdominal surgery patients

raw.rationale: The patient's condition deteriorated with high fever, elevated WBC count, and positive blood culture with Gram-negative bacteria, which are indicative of sepsis due to gram-negative bacteria.

rejected.label: Postoperative peritonitis
rejected.why: While the patient had peritonitis, the presence of Gram-negative bacteria in the blood culture suggests a more systemic infection, namely sepsis.

rejected.label: Intra-abdominal abscess
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence of an abscess, and the patient's symptoms and lab results are more consistent with a systemic infection.

rejected.label: Bacteroides fragilis infection
rejected.why: The Gram stain and culture results do not specifically identify Bacteroides fragilis, and the 16S rRNA sequencing did not match this species.

rejected.label: Enterococcal peritonitis
rejected.why: The Gram stain showed Gram-negative bacteria, which contradicts the diagnosis of Enterococcal peritonitis, as Enterococci are Gram-positive bacteria.
